discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 229051e. The writer now lives behind its own per-session mutex; terminal_write takes the sessions lock only to clone that handle, then releases it before the blocking write_all. kill and kill_all only need the sessions lock.

Fair, the per-session lock alone still let a blocked write_all stall the sync IPC command thread. 939760a moves the write off that thread entirely: each session now owns a writer thread fed by an unbounded mpsc channel, and terminal_write only enqueues. Dropping the session (kill/exit) drops the sender and the thread ends; a write blocked on a shell that stopped reading returns EIO once the shell is killed and the PTY closes. Verified live: a 200KB pipe plus kill stays responsive.

Good catch. The webview never reuses a tab id (each tab gets a fresh id and spawns at most once), so this was theoretical, but the defensive replace path made it reachable in principle. 69265482b tags each session with a generation and the reader only removes the entry if the map still holds its own generation.

Valid, fixed in 8e4ae4f. Added a terminal_kill_all command that the webview calls on load, and the terminal is only offered once that resolves, so a panel restored after the reload cannot have its fresh shell caught by the reap. Verified live: started sleep in a tab, reloaded the webview, the orphaned process was gone and the restored panel came back with a new live shell.

Addressed in 74f6a0c4dd. Both installers now recheck the installed build epoch while holding the installation lock, immediately before replacing the executable. The native CLI exposes a build-epoch probe and releases publish a matching metadata sidecar for cross-target caches. Added a locked downgrade rejection test that confirms the existing executable remains unchanged.
